title: KoshiReach: Flood-Induced Rural Accessibility Modelling and Emergency Resource Optimization
abstract: A proposed geospatial research framework investigating how flood-induced disruption of rural transportation networks affects access to healthcare and how limited emergency resources can be allocated to reduce accessibility inequality in Bihar. The study will combine graph-based accessibility modelling, spatial data integration and constrained mathematical optimization.
content:
## Research Motivation

Flooding can disrupt transportation infrastructure, isolate rural populations and restrict access to essential healthcare services. Flood extent maps alone do not establish the resulting changes in accessibility.

## Primary Research Question

How does flood-induced disruption of rural road networks affect population access to healthcare, and how can limited emergency resources be allocated to minimize accessibility inequality?

## Proposed Methodology

- Integrate historical flood extents, road networks, healthcare facilities and population estimates within a bounded study region.
- Construct geographically referenced transportation graphs and establish baseline accessibility using shortest-path algorithms.
- Simulate flood-related edge disruptions and estimate accessibility losses.
- Investigate facility-location and maximum-coverage optimization against heuristic baselines.
- Evaluate uncertainty in road disruption scenarios.

## Candidate Datasets

Global Flood Database, PMGSY GeoSadak, OpenStreetMap, WorldPop and optional Sentinel-1 observations. Actual coverage, licensing, completeness and suitability remain subject to verification.

## Proposed Technology Stack

Python, GeoPandas, OSMnx, NetworkX, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Google OR-Tools, FastAPI and MapLibre GL. Technology selection remains provisional.

## Evaluation Strategy

Travel time, population coverage, accessibility inequality, estimated isolated populations, allocation efficiency, solver runtime and sensitivity to uncertain road failures.

## Expected Deliverables

A reproducible spatial analysis pipeline, comparative optimization experiments, documented limitations and an interactive research visualization.

## Current Status and Limitations

Development has not started. No experimental results or implemented technologies are claimed. Inferred road disruptions will be distinguished from verified closures, and research outputs will not be presented as operational emergency navigation guidance.
